title: Children’s Engineering Workshops
transcript:
Speaker 0: IELTS 16. Published by Cambridge University Press and Cambridge Assessment English 2021. This recording is copyright. Test one. This is the IELTS listening test. You will hear a number of different recordings, and you will have to answer questions on what you hear. There will be time for you to read the instructions and questions, and you will have a chance to check your work. All the recordings will be played once only. The test is in four parts. At the end of the test, you will be given ten minutes to transfer your answers to the answer sheet. Now turn to part one. Part one. You will hear a man phoning to find out about some children's engineering workshops. First, you have some time to look at questions one to three. Now listen carefully and answer questions one to three.
Speaker 1: Hello. Children's engineering workshops.
Speaker 2: Oh, hello. I wanted some information about the workshops in the school holidays.
Speaker 1: Sure.
Speaker 2: I have two daughters who are interested. The younger one's Lydia. She's four. Do you take children as young as that?
Speaker 1: Yes. Our tiny engineers workshop is for four to five year olds.
Speaker 2: What sorts of activities do they do?
Speaker 1: All sorts. For example, they work together to design a special cover that goes round an egg so that when it's inside, they can drop it from a height and it doesn't break. Well, sometimes it does break, but that's part of the fun.
Speaker 2: Right. And Lydia loves building things. Is there any opportunity for her to do that?
Speaker 1: Well, they have a competition to see who can make the highest tower. You'd be amazed how high they can
Speaker 2: go. Right.
Speaker 1: But they're learning all the time as well as having fun. For example, one thing they do is to design and build a car that's attached to a balloon, and the force of the air in that actually powers the car and makes it move along. They go really fast too.
Speaker 2: Okay. Well, all this sounds perfect.
Speaker 0: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions four to 10. Now listen and answer questions four to 10.
Speaker 2: Now Carly, that's my older daughter, has just had her seventh birthday. So presumably, she'd be in a different group.
Speaker 1: Yes. She'd be in the junior engineers. That's for children from six to eight.
Speaker 2: And do they do the same sorts of activities?
Speaker 1: Some are the same, but a bit more advanced. So they work out how to build model vehicles, things like cars and trucks, but also how to construct animals using the same sorts of material and technique. And then they learn how they can program them and make them move.
Speaker 2: So they learn a bit of coding?
Speaker 1: They do. They pick it up really quickly. We're there to help if they need it, but they learn from one another too.
Speaker 2: Right. And do they have competitions too?
Speaker 1: Yes. With the junior engineers, it's to use recycled materials like card and wood to build a bridge, and the longest one gets a prize.
Speaker 2: That sounds fun. I wouldn't mind doing that myself.
Speaker 1: Then they have something a bit different, which is to think up an idea for a five minute movie and then film it using special animation software. You'd be amazed what they come up with.
Speaker 2: And, of course, that's something they can put on their phone and take home to show all their friends.
Speaker 1: Exactly. And then they also build a robot in the shape of a human, and they decorate it and program it so that it can move its arms and legs.
Speaker 2: Perfect. So is it the same price as the tiny engineers?
Speaker 1: It's just a bit more, £50 for the five weeks.
Speaker 2: And are the classes on a Monday too?
Speaker 1: They used to be, but we found it didn't give our staff enough time to clear up after the first workshop, so we moved them to Wednesdays. The classes are held in the morning from ten to eleven.
Speaker 2: Okay. That's better for me, actually. And what about the location? Where exactly are the workshops held?
Speaker 1: They're in Building 10 A. There's a big sign on the door. You can't miss it, and that's in Fradstone Industrial Estate.
Speaker 2: Sorry?
Speaker 1: Fradstone. That's F R A D S T 0 N E.
Speaker 2: And that's in Grassford, isn't it?
Speaker 1: Yes. Or past the station.
Speaker 2: And will I have any parking problems there?
Speaker 1: No. There's always plenty available. So would you like to enroll Lydia and Carly now?
Speaker 2: Okay.
Speaker 1: So can I have your full name and
Speaker 0: That is the end of part one? You now have half a minute to check your answers to part one.
